The Friends alum revealed that she was approached about directing Evil Genius , her first feature film as a director in 12 years, after accidentally running into Barbara Schroeder, who directed the Netflix documentary of the same name, at the iconic hotel in Beverly Hills. “I was at the Beverly Hills Hotel sitting at the counter; my favorite spot in the corner. I saw [Schroeder], and I was like, ‘Oh my God, I love Evil Genius . You did such a great job,’” Cox said at The Hollywood Reporter ’s Studio at 1 Hotel during TIFF , presented by sponsor Canada Goose. “She said, ‘It’s available to direct.’ She goes, ‘You should run with it.’ We had a good relationship before. … I made a lot of deals there [at the Beverly Hills Hotel], and made a lot of money there. It’s just interesting.” Related Stories TV Josh Hartnett Reveals He Was "Actively Not Looking to Do a TV Show" Before Joining 'Below' Movies Sebastian Stan Says "Invitation to Be Negative" in Society "Starts at the Top": "It's Just So Lazy" Cox jokingly added that those deals were always “at the counter”: “I can’t get inside the poker room.” Cox’s chance encounter sparked the idea to direct, but it took years to get Evil Genius off the ground. The Scream star told THR that the film was in development for “eight years” through the COVID-19 lockdown and the 2023 WGA and SAG-AFTRA strikes before going into production in 2025. Despite facing significant obstacles, Cox “couldn’t let [the story] go because I loved it.” The film, which stars Patricia Arquette, David Harbour, Michael Chernus, Garret Dillahunt and Danielle Macdonald, follows the true crime story of the 2003 “pizza bomber” case that resulted in the death of Brian Wells. “We got these two amazing actors,” Cox said, referencing Arquette and Harbour, who also visited THR ’s studio on Friday. “I knew there was a story beneath the headlines that was really emotional and touching and terrifying and all of the things, and I’ve got the best actors to play the parts.” Cox was joined by her daughter, Coco, and Arquette’s daughter, Harlow, who both have small parts in the film. The Shining Vale actor told THR that Coco loves to perform. “Coco, she’s got a little scene in the movie, and Harlow, Patricia’s daughter, is young Marge,” Cox said. “Coco’s really sweet, too. … Coco loves acting so much that she was so happy to be there. It’s amazing.” “She’s been studying since she was so little, and doing shows and plays,” Arquette added of Coco. “She’s the only one… well, her and David, who did a lot of musical theater, and all of this. She just finished her first other movie. So, it’s very exciting. They’re fifth-generation actresses, our little daughters.” Evil Genius premieres at TIFF on Saturday, Sept. 12. THR

title: ‘The View’s Sunny Hostin Defends AI As “New Art Form” Amid “Gatekeeping In Hollywood Around Black & Brown Creative Content”
full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Ocean Way Festival Canceled In Santa Monica Due To Beach Erosion & “Can No Longer Be Safely Held As Planned” Gary Oldman Says HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series Will Be “More Satisfying” Than The Movies ‘The View’s Sunny Hostin Defends AI As “New Art Form” Amid “Gatekeeping In Hollywood Around Black & Brown Creative Content” View All September 11, 2026 6:52pm (L-R) Joy Behar, Sunny Hostin and Alyssa Farah Griffin Sunny Hostin received pushback from her co-hosts on The View as she defended the use of AI in Hollywood. Hostin, who recently licensed her name and likeness to AI company Fountain 0, argued that generative AI should be considered a “new art form,” noting that it can help the entertainment industry show more Black and Brown representation. “I partnered with this company because I’ve written a trilogy, and for six years I’ve tried to get my films or my stories made into series and films, and the gatekeeping in Hollywood around Black and Brown creative content is insane,” the former prosecutor said. “I cannot get New York Times best-selling books onto the screen to tell diverse stories to diverse communities.” Related Stories News ‘The View’ Season 30 Cast Photos & Guests Set For ABC Talk Show News ‘The View’s Whoopi Goldberg Shuts Down Audience Boos At Ted Cruz Mention: “We Don’t Jell With Them Always, But We Are Respectful” She continued, “With AI, that cuts out the gatekeeping. You get to make your film. You get to have a director … It’s a way to go to a streamer and say, ‘Here’s the product. Will you license it? Will you show it?’ It’s a way, I think, to get Black and Brown stories told.” Watch on Deadline Joy Behar noted that with AI, “real people are not working,” and Hostin added, “The real people are not getting jobs in Hollywood. Black and Brown actors are not getting the jobs.” Alyssa Farah Griffin jumped on Behar’s point and said, “I worry you’re closing the doors to those roles being played by Black and Brown actors and being replaced by AI.” “That would be great if the studios would not gatekeep and allow the stories to be told,” Hostin replied. Griffin also said generative AI is “pulling from intellectual property of all the existing actors out there,” and they aren’t getting residuals for it. One thing that’s for sure is that the AI “train has left the station,” as Hostin said, who added, “This is something that’s here. It’s not going away, and I think that there are going to be enormous benefits.” Ana Navarro asked Hostin whether she felt any ethical issues with working with an AI company, and Hostin said she “thought about it a lot” before signing away her likeness. “I think that diverse stories need to be told,” Hostin said before Behar interjected to say, “We’ve said that already. I’m saying that those same people that you’re worried about are now out of work.” Hostin defended that point, saying, “I’m not the person putting them out of work because the studios just won’t make these projects.” Behar then said, “Force them to do it rather than have a robot replace Black people in movies.” Hostin closed out the topic, saying, “I don’t think it’s ever going to take away the arts. I think it’s a different art form.” Watch the full exchange from The View in the video below. ‘Practical Magic 2’ Conjuring $30M U.S.; NFL Week 1 To Impact Holdovers Company & State AGs Set Antitrust Suit Settlement Talks For October Noah Reid To Headline CBS’ ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff, Will Guest On Cop Show ‘Onwards And Sideways’ Chat; ‘Girl Group’, ‘River’, ‘Stuffed’ Reviews; WB Chiefs Read More About: 7 Comments

title: Sydney Sweeney Faces Backlash for Sexualized Novig Ad: “Exactly Why Women in Sports Aren’t Taken Seriously”
full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All September 11, 2026 6:50pm Sydney Sweeney’s Novig ad Novig More than a year after her American Eagle ad controversy, Sydney Sweeney is facing backlash for another campaign: her sexualized promotion for sports trading app Novig. The Euphoria actress partnered up with Novig on Wednesday to support the new platform, which launched last month. She not only starred in the ad but also joined Novig as a strategic partner and equity holder. Novig’s “platform combines the mechanics of modern financial exchanges with a sports-first experience, creating a more efficient and transparent way for fans to trade on sports outcomes,” per a release. It’s also dubbed “the only prediction market to maintain a 21+ age requirement,” which the brand argues “[sets] a higher standard for responsible participation as the category continues to grow.” Related Stories THR + Sportico: Game Recognize Game Belmont Cameli and NHL Phenom Macklin Celebrini Talk 'Off Campus,' Olympic Heartbreak and Handling the Hype Lifestyle Sydney Sweeney Stars in Provocative Ad Campaign for Novig Sports Trading App Some users are arguing Sweeney’s ad for the age-restricted platform could have used an R-rated rating as well. “I couldn’t believe when that ad came on the tv. I had my 2 children in the living room I had to yell at them to look away from the TV. I don’t understand WHY they would need to create such a [vulgar] ad,” a TikTok user commented on a post made by Marissa Womack, manager of game day promotions and programming for minor league baseball team the Harrisburg Senators. Others took to Sweeney’s Instagram comments , including one user who called out Instagram’s inconsistencies with taking down potentially sexualized content. “Love how @instagram allows for stuff like this but the moment I post something in a bikini , the post is removed,” they wrote, while another added, “22.4 million views but not even 1 million likes… why? Because this is not what we want for our sports ads. ESPECIALLY when kids like and follow sports as well.” Other descriptors for the ad in the Anyone But You star’s comments include “disgusting,” “pathetic,” “sad” and “inappropriate.” The Hollywood Reporter reached out to reps for Novig and Sweeney for comment but did not hear back by the time of publication. Womack explained her frustration with the ad in her TikTok video, calling out the representation of women in the sports industry. “This [criticism] isn’t about me being jealous or insecure of [Sweeney]. … it’s about the fact that this is already a male-dominated field where we are constantly having to prove why we belong. it’s about having passions and joy working in this industry and when the only representation is sexualization, you see less and less young women wanting to pursue this industry!” The campaign, in Sweeney’s own words, “was about embracing a fun idea.” She added in a statement, “The concept is simple: cut through the noise and put the focus entirely on sports. The campaign brings that idea to life with confidence, humor and a playful edge.” The only “sports” that are featured in the ad, however, are different balls and uniforms placed provocatively on top of Sweeney’s mostly naked body. One TikTok user directly criticized the sexualization of the actress in the ad in the comments of a video shared by Sam Tirelli, a studio/field director for a Maryland-based sports network: “There is 0 reason to have somebody naked just saying sports over and over again. You can make amazing ads and content without constantly having women be sexualized.” Many users also slammed the ad for being “exactly why women in sports aren’t taken seriously,” one TikToker argued. They also called out the notion that “they probably knew it was going to be controversial too,” with The Housemaid star being known to spark controversy through brand advertisements. Most prominently, her viral 2025 American Eagle jeans ad caused widespread backlash , partly due to a piece of the advert where Sweeney said, “Genes are passed down from parents to offspring, often determining traits like hair color, personality and even eye color. My jeans are blue.” Some people argued that the campaign tagline “Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans” was a play on the term “great jeans” versus “great genes” and claimed the ad promoted eugenics. The ad garnered so much online backlash at the time that it prompted American Eagle to respond , releasing a statement that read in part, “Sydney Sweeney Has Great Jeans is and always was about the jeans. Her jeans. Her story.” Sweeney has addressed the controversy numerous times, saying that “the reaction definitely was a surprise.” She later commented on the cultural conversation that arose with the American Eagle ad, with a Cosmopolitan interviewer asking her about being labeled “MAGA Barbie,” as she’s repeatedly said she does not want to address her personal politics. “I’ve never been here to talk about politics. I’ve always been here to make art, so this is just not a conversation I want to be at the forefront of,” Sweeney said. When asked in the same interview if she sees herself confirming her political beliefs in the future, she said, “No.” Sweeney added, “I’m not a political person. I’m in the arts. I’m not here to speak on politics. That’s not an area I’ve ever even imagined getting into. It’s not why I became who I am. I became an actor because I like to tell stories, but I don’t believe in hate in any form.” Sweeney also made sure to note that politics were not to be bet on when trading on Novig. “No betting on wars or deaths, and no politics,” she said, before a clip of her from behind and masking her breast with only her hand was shown, as she adds, “Just you, your takes and sports.” A mini logline provided in a press release for the Novig ad reads, “Ahead of football season, Sydney Sweeney is putting the focus exactly where it belongs, on ‘Just Sports.'” However, that “focus” is now anywhere but sports and instead back onto another conversation-starting ad led by the two-time Emmy nominee. THR

title: Josh Hartnett Reveals He Was “Actively Not Looking to Do a TV Show” Before Joining ‘Below’
full_text: Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Mariel Turner Plus Icon Mariel Turner View All September 11, 2026 6:25pm Logo text Josh Hartnett was happy to continue his career on the big screen before Below came his way. The Oppenheimer actor revealed on Friday that was “actively not looking” for television roles before reading the script of the Netflix thriller miniseries, created and written by Jesse McKeown. “Can I just say I was actively not looking to do a TV show?” Harnett shared at The Hollywood Reporter ’s Studio at 1 Hotel during Toronto International Film Festival , presented by sponsor Canada Goose. “Like, I was actively not looking for this. I’d just came off a movie and wanted to do another movie. I was going to go do another movie, and then I read this [script], and I was like, ‘Wow, this is amazing.’” Related Stories Movies Sorry, Caleb Hearon Is Not Your Clown in 'Trash Mountain' Grief Dramedy Movies Courteney Cox Says She Decided to Direct 'Evil Genius' After Chance Encounter at the Beverly Hills Hotel: "I Made a Lot of Deals There" Set in a remote Newfoundland fishing village, Below follows Hartnett’s Calvin as he fights to protect his family and community from a mysterious, terrifying sea creature. The series, which also stars Charlie Heaton, Mackenzie Davis and Natasha Henstridge, has been compared to Apple TV’s comedy horror hit Widow’s Bay , but Hartnett sees a distinct difference between the two shows. “ I saw Widow’s Bay and I really liked it, but there’s a totally different tone in this show,” he explained. “It’s much more sort of human-oriented and less sort of overtly comedic, but very funny in its own way.” Below was filmed on location in St. John’s, Newfoundland, Canada, where Hartnett learned the unique Canadian accent and lived like a local. The Verity actor told THR that he often frequented restaurants in town (“I love The Duke. It’s a great pub”) and did his best “not to hit [a] moose” while driving. Hartnett and Heaton worked with a dialect coach to perfect the Newfoundland accent. “ Charlie and I play father and son, and we are clearly from the same place. We had to find the specific sounds that we were gonna use for our family accent,” the actor said. “Newfoundland is not — there’s not a lot of people, but it’s a very large land mass, and there are lots of people that have been there for generations in one place. [They have] very specific dialects, and there’s many of them. We had to choose which one was gonna work best, I think, for the family, and then all work together … We were able to do that, which was really cool, and we had a great dialect coach.” Hartnett added that he listened to The Broadcast , a long-running radio show on CBC, “almost every day” to master the accent “because [there] was so many regional dialects.” While his character in Below may be fearless in the water, Harnett has a decidingly different view. “I was born in 1978, like [when] Jaws [was popular],” the actor dished. “[I’m] terrified of the water.” Below debuts on Netflix on Oct. 8. THR

title: Pink Issues Statement Following Backlash for Critiquing Macklemore’s Pro-Palestine Comments: “Standing Up for My Own People”
full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All September 11, 2026 6:08pm P!NK attends The 79th Annual Tony Awards at Radio City Music Hall on June 07, 2026 in New York City. Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for Tony Awards Productions Pink issued an extensive statement on Friday addressing the backlash she faced for resharing a post calling out Macklemore for his pro-Palestine comments and demanding he be removed from Ed Sheeran’s ongoing tour. In a lengthy post on Instagram Friday, the singer-songwriter said that the post she had shared “said things in words I didn’t write, and I wouldn’t have chosen all of them,” further stating that “I’d rather be disagreed with for what I actually said than hated for what anybody else wrote, so let me say it.” “I was born a Jew. I didn’t pick it, and I’ve never hidden it,” she wrote. “And this week a whole lot of people decided what I believe without asking me, without checking a single thing I’ve ever said or done, because a repost and the word ‘Jew’ were apparently enough to fill in the rest. But let me fill it in… myself.” Related Stories Music Snoop Dogg Tapped to Host the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards Music Noah Kahan Drops "Orbiter" Music Video on Spotify View this post on Instagram “Of course I don’t speak for Israel, or for any government,” she continued. “I never have. What I said in October 2023 is still exactly what I believe: Hamas is a terrorist organization. Palestinians deserve a future that honors their humanity and their aspirations. Protecting innocent life comes first, everywhere, and nobody should ever celebrate the death of a child. Anybody’s child. I’ve spent a decade as a UNICEF ambassador for kids who didn’t choose the country or the war they were born into, and I have grieved every one of them, on both sides of that fence. I didn’t do it from behind a screen; I went to those children and held them. I’m not going to litigate a complex war in an Instagram caption, and I’m not going to recite anybody’s slogan to earn back a follower.” P!nk responds to backlash after she shared a post labelling Macklemore as “anti-Israel” for spreading awareness about Palestine: “Last Sunday I reposted somebody else's post about Macklemore's set at Ed Sheeran's show. It said things in words I didn't write, and I wouldn't have… pic.twitter.com/tAixSCFTRG — Pop Base (@PopBase) September 11, 2026 She continued her post in her comment section, though it appears much of her statement was removed after she limited comments on the post. Her statement in full is still available in screenshots online, including in the X post above. Regarding Macklemore specifically, she recalled the rapper wearing a costume during a performance back in 2014 that was widely criticized at the time as antisemitic. He apologized, saying that “I respect all cultures and all people.” “Every Jew I know knew exactly what it was,” Pink wrote Friday. “But he apologized, and I let it go, because that’s what we do. We let it go. Then last weekend he stood in front of a stadium full of music -loving families, with violent images from a war on the screens, dedicated a song to the movement of his choice, and then took the mic to tell all of the Jews in the stadium that it wasn’t about them. You don’t get to decide that for us.” “That’s what prompted my repost,” Pink continued. “Not ‘Free Palestine,’ and not anyone’s right to say it. I have never asked for another artist to be silenced and I’m not asking now. I don’t need anyone fired, and I don’t need a refund. What I need is to be able to say, as a Jewish mom, that scared me, and it scared people I love, without being told our fear is just propaganda, and without being told I’m somehow cool with genocide because I noticed?” Pink further said she was “standing up for my own people, and I thought I knew going in how lonely that would be. And it’s lonelier than that. But I’m doing it anyway.” She wrote that the phrase “zionist” has become a “slur by people who couldn’t tell you the details of what I believe.” She concluded her post in remembrance of today’s 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks and for the start of Rosh Hashanah, finishing with a “shana tova” for the Jewish new year. Macklemore courted controversy last week during his opening set on Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for his Free Palestine messaging, with the Israeli-American Council subsequently sharing a petition calling to have him removed from the tour. During his set last Saturday, the rapper further continued with his Free Palestine message, further saying on stage that “to all of my Jewish brothers and sisters: Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you.” The rapper doubled down further on Monday, writing on social media that “wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial.” Wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial. pic.twitter.com/BOJ9xMoIZn — Macklemore (@macklemore) September 7, 2026 THR

title: Russell Crowe Charms 1,400-Strong Venice Audience With ‘What Love Builds’ Doc Charting His Musical Career
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Russell Crowe Charms 1,400-Strong Venice Audience With ‘What Love Builds’ Doc Charting His Musical Career ‘Before The War’, ‘Our Share Of Sand’ Scoop Top Venice Critics’ Week Prizes Venice Parallel Section Giornate Degli Autori Unveils 2026 Winners View All September 11, 2026 5:10pm Russell Crowe and Alberto Barbera at the What Love Builds world premiere at the Venice Film Festival Vittorio Zunino Celotto/Getty Images Russell Crowe enjoyed an enthusiastic response to his bio-doc meets concert film What Love Builds as it premiered Out of Competition to a 1,400-strong crowd at the Venice Film Festival on Friday evening. The documentary sets out to show that music has been part of Crowes’s life long before he decided to move to Sydney from New Zealand in the late 1980s to pursue an acting career, busking on the streets initially to make ends meet. It charts Crowe’s early musical endeavours from his teen years performing at an Auckland music hall under the stage name of Russ Le Roq, to his 415 performances as Eddie/Dr Scott in a New Zealand production of The Rocky Horror Show . Related Stories News International Insider: European TV In Peril; Venice & TIFF Latest; Mercedes Ron Interview Festivals 'Before The War', 'Our Share Of Sand' Scoop Top Venice Critics' Week Prizes Crowe delves into the creation of his first major band 30 Odd Foot of Grunts in 1992; its prophetic The Photograph Kills EP , and his abrupt decision to disband it as his acting career took off and he felt his fame was muddying the waters. He suggested a pushy offer verging on the vampiric from then Sony head Tommy Mottola to sign the band had been the final straw. Watch on Deadline In an example of how his love of music has fed into his acting, Crowe reveals how a line in Gladiator from his character Maximus in which he tells Emperor Marcus Aurelius that he has been away for “2 years, 264 days, and this morning” had been written at his request and taken inspiration from the “It’s been seven hours and 15 days” lyric in Prince’s track Nothing Compares 2 U. Later, he recounts how on 2010 Robin Hood , he had been able to influence the casting of the merry men to bring in actors who were also musicians. These would include Scott Grimes who would go on to become an occasional member of his current band Indoor Garden Party alongside the likes of Les Misérables actress Samantha Barks and Canadian folk rock musician Alan Doyle. Crowe also digs into lows of his career such as his arrest in New York in 2005 for assault for throwing a telephone at a hotel employee; “the pain” of being pursued by paparazzi, to whom he says he is ironically also grateful for capturing some of his favorite pictures of him with his children, or the ridiculing of his work as a musician and songwriter as his fame took off. Footage from the band’s performances intercut throughout film had the Venice audience clapping as if in a concert, with a cover version by Crowe of Dire Straits’ Romeo and Juliet causing the Sala Darsena theater to erupt into full-scale applause. Russell Crowe breaks into huge smile as 1,400-strong crowd claps to the beat of closing credits of bio-doc come concert film ‘What Love Builds’ at Venice Film Festival pic.twitter.com/zEO5ho8WNa — Deadline (@DEADLINE) September 11, 2026 As the credits rolled at the end, spectators clapped to the beat of the final track while a visibly happy Crowe laughed and smiled at the reaction. Crowe, who wrote, directed and produced the documentary, told a press conference earlier that it had been 15 years in the making. “I thought it might take me a year, but as I was doing it, things would come up that I was going to be doing shortly with the music, so I kept waiting for that, and the next thing, and the next thing. By the time we sat down to cut it we had an extensive 18 feet of film,” he said. “It was massive undertaking to try to chip away at the narrative, but I knew what my intention was, and my intention was to answer the question I get asked probably most and that is to define the difference between music and acting. The film attempts to explain the two things are completely intertwined for me,” he said. Crowe said Venice had been his target festival for the documentary and revealed he had contacted Italian director Gabriele Muccino, who directed him in Fathers & Daughters , to help connect him with Artistic Director Alberto Barbera. “As we’re coming towards the end of the cut, I said out loud, the most amazing thing would be if I could get to screen this in Venice. I’ve been to a lot of film festivals, but the most fun film festival is Venice, and there’s depth in the appreciation of the audience,” he said. “I couldn’t have had a better result as a filmmaker. title: ‘60 Minutes’ to Tackle Trump Pardons in Season Premiere
full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All September 11, 2026 4:51pm '60 Minutes' correspondent Lesley Stahl with Donald Trump. Courtesy of CBS News/'60 Minutes' The 59th season premiere of 60 Minutes will dedicate a segment to Donald Trump’s controversial use of the presidential pardon. The segment is the third and final segment to be revealed from the premiere episode, following Jon Wertheim’s profile of the Los Angeles Rams and coach Sean McVay, and Norah O’Donnell’s exclusive interview with the U.S. pilot who was shot down and rescued in Iran. But it is Lesley Stahl’s segment, “The Pardon Economy,” that may end up raising the most eyebrows. “Presidents have pardoned criminals since the time of George Washington. It’s a constitutional power that has been controversial from the start — but perhaps never more so than during the Trump presidency,” the description states. “Lesley Stahl and 60 Minutes investigate the world of lawyers and lobbyists who have created a new pardon economy. Shachar Bar-On and Michael Kaplan are the producers.” 60 Minutes is in flux. New executive producer Nick Bilton is working with returning correspondents Stahl, Bill Whitaker, Wertheim and O’Donnell, as well as a handful of new hires, to try and get the season off the ground following an exodus of talent, both voluntary departures and forced ones. Former CBS News chief Wendy McMahon predicted that the season premiere will be a “banger” this week, betting that the show will put its best foot forward to try and set the tone, but that “shows three, four, and five could get quite interesting, I think.” Any segment targeting Trump, who sued CBS over a 60 Minutes interview with Vice President Kamala Harris, is sure to attract extra scrutiny. While the first show will be familiar, Bilton is expected to change things over time, with hidden camera investigations, and perhaps end-of show segments featuring commentary or debate, all cited as potential additions. For now, however, the show is leaning on the familiar: Stahl, O’Donnell and Wertheim are all veterans of the program. The new faces and other changes will wait until future episodes. THR

full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Curry Barker Initially Planned To Get Tattoos If ‘Obsession’ Opened To $20M; Inde Navarrette Has Plans To Direct – TIFF United Artists, Amazon MGM & Steven Spielberg’s ‘Mandela Catalogue’ Sets Summer 2028 Release Warner Bros’ Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy On Gen-Z Resurge, Credibility With Filmmakers & Embracing The Unknown – Toronto View All September 11, 2026 3:57pm Curry Barker And Inde Navarrette Getty Images “All we can hope for is that it sustains” That’s what Curry Barker was first told by his reps and those around him about the domestic box office prospects for his horror pic Obsession . He wasn’t expecting too much. Then the horror romance wound up making more than Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu , $512.6M to $345.5M at the global box office. In a sit-down at TIFF with his leading Obsession star Inde Navarrette, moderated by the fest’s Midnight Madness programmer Peter Kuplowsky, the duo reminisced how their lives have changed over the last year following the pic’s world premiere at TIFF where it was snatched up by Focus Features for $15M. The first change they noticed was an upgrade in their flight and hotel this year versus last when they arrived as a pure indie ( Obsession was financed by Capstone for $750K). Related Stories Reviews Toronto Film Festival 2026: Read All Of Deadline's Reviews Reviews 'Faith' Review: Erin Doherty Is Heartbreaking As A Mother On The Brink In Paul Andrew Williams' Soulful Supernatural Drama - Toronto Film Festival However, had Obsession opened to $20M, Barker shared there was a plan for him and his reps to get tattoos. Watch on Deadline “It didn’t (do that). It made $17M. So we’re like ‘Ok, I guess we’re not getting the tattoos…still really cool’,” he said, “And then the next weekend it made $27M. It was like ‘Holy shit!’ That’s unheard of for it to go up!.” Interesting backstory, Barker had Obsession tested and the audience was quite unhappy with Bear (Michael Johnston) and his handling of off-the-rails g.f. Nikki (Navarrette), who he put a love-binding toxic spell on. “People were saying that they were frustrated with Bear and they didn’t understand why he doesn’t just try to do more to fix it (the spell.” “They were like ‘Why isn’t he going back to the crystal shop? Why isn’t he doing more research and trying to fix it?’ We got an overwhelming amount of people wanting us to do that,” said the filmmaker. “Then I was like ‘Oh, wait, that’s not what I want to do. I don’t want to try and fix it. It’s way more interesting that there’s a passivity in his character. He’s what I would call a passive antagonist,” explained Barker. “So, it became clear to me that the way to fix the movie was not to make Bear try and fix it sooner, but to actually make it even more clear to the audience that he wants to make it work. That’s the thing that he becomes active on trying to make this work,” said Barker. Barker thus had reshoots, which he praised his financier for; those additional resources proved to the filmmaker that his backers had complete faith in his vision. In regards to his how his career changed: Barker no longer gets ‘Nos’ when he heads into pitch meetings. Before Obsession, he would constantly come up with new ideas which were shot down. Now, the response he gets is, “‘Curry, what is it you want to do?'” shared the director. “It’s a little more challenging, he added, “I can pitch anything.” In terms of Navarrette’s streak, she recently appeared at D23 where it was announced she’s playing Rogue in the Marvel Studio’s revival of X-Men. “Everything has changed for me, I’m now in rooms I could never even imagine,” said Navarrette about her life post TIFF 2025, “I’m pitching my own projects and am hopefully can produce and direct my own stuff.” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Conjuring $30M U.S.; NFL Week 1 To Impact Holdovers Company & State AGs Set Antitrust Suit Settlement Talks For October Noah Reid To Headline CBS’ ‘Sheriff Country’ Medical Spinoff, Will Guest On Cop Show ‘Onwards And Sideways’ Chat; ‘Girl Group’, ‘River’, ‘Stuffed’ Reviews; WB Chiefs Read More About: 2 Comments

The decision comes a month and a half after Season 2 was released on July 23. Ransom Canyon , an adaptation of the Jodi Thomas novels, already was on borrowed time. Related Stories Recaps ‘Ransom Canyon’ Showrunner Breaks Down Season 2: Grift, Love Triangles, Surprise Pregnancy & Ending That Is “Launch Of Next Story” For Possible Season 3 Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Cancellations Photo Gallery: Series Ending This Year & Beyond After a respectable but not massive viewership for Season 1, the series found itself somewhat on the bubble last year. It was eventually renewed for Season 2 more than two months after the premiere with a reduced order (eight episodes vs. 10) and a creative overhaul that included a supporting cast shakeup. With the storyline reset and other major changes, I hear the second installment was creatively better received internally. But, following a similar trajectory as many Netflix sophomore shows recently, Ransom Canyon returned down , logging 4.1 million views for its first week of release, off 43% from its Season 1 opening week, which collected 7.2 million views. Watch on Deadline The drama managed to bring its first season back into Netflix’s Top 10 for a week, which is important to the streamer, but the new installment fell off the Top 10 after only three weeks vs. four for Season 1. With Netflix weighing cost vs. performance for its renewal decisions, the Season 2 viewership likely was not enough to secure another season for a show that has considerable budget given its marquee-name leads. One of the things for which Ransom Canyon will be remembered is that Kelly stood her ground and asked for pay parity with Duhamel when she was offered the co-lead opposite him in 2022. It was a bold move amid a post-pandemic, post-peak TV industry contraction but it paid off — as Deadline reported last year , while she did not achieve full parity, Kelly came close to it and praised Netflix for their response to her request. Other sophomore Netflix series this year with similar or bigger year-to-year premiere week viewership slides that have managed to secure third seasons include Running Point (-43%), The Four Seasons (-63%) and several shows that had been renewed ahead of their Season 2 debuts including The Gentlemen (-45%), Avatar: The Last Airbender (-59%) and A Good Girl’s Guide To Murder (-76%). Netflix series to recently score a renewal also include Tires, My Life With the Walter Boys, Free Bert and Big Mistakes. Ransom Canyon follows childhood friends-turned-star-crossed lovers Staten Kirkland (Duhamel) and Quinn O’Grady (Kelly) who never seem to be able to get their timing right. The duo were tested again in the second season with Quinn getting briefly engaged to someone else but by the end, unlike the Season 1 finale which saw Staten and Quinn split up, they were in a good place — and very much together. In fact, as opposed as Season 1, the Season 2 closer of Random Canyon did not have any jaw-dropping cliffhangers, which would bring some consolation to fans who had invested in the series and its characters for two seasons. The finale did set up a potential love triangle for Ellie (Marianly Tejada) and a possible larger Season 3 presence for Staten’s half-brother Levi, played by Steve Howey, who deserved more than the single scene he was in. In Season 2 of Ransom Canyon , the titular Texas town hangs in the balance as ranching dynasties unravel, hearts switch allegiances and the overall future of small town culture built on ranching and agriculture comes under scrutiny. full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Practical Magic 2’ Conjuring $30M U.S. Opening – Box Office Update United Artists, Amazon MGM & Steven Spielberg’s ‘Mandela Catalogue’ Sets Summer 2028 Release Warner Bros’ Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy On Gen-Z Resurge, Credibility With Filmmakers & Embracing The Unknown – Toronto View All July 7, 2026 7:00am TIFF The Toronto Film Festival said Tuesday that Apple Original Films’ Being Heumann from Oscar-winning CODA filmmaker Siân Heder will be the opening-night film of TIFF ‘s 51st edition in the fall. In addition, two other world premieres — Prima Facie from British director Susanna White starring three-time Oscar nominee Cynthia Erivo, and The Assassin(s) from Korean filmmaker Hur Jin-ho ( A Normal Family , TIFF ’23) — have been set for this year’s TIFF, which runs September 10-20. Related Stories Festivals Details Of Toronto Film Festival’s C$23M Market Revealed: Name & Dates Set As More Heavyweight Industry Advisors Join Ahead Of 2026 Launch Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Being Heumann stars BAFTA Award nominee Ruth Madeley ( Don’t Take My Baby ) as famed disability activist Judy Heumann in what is a feature take of her bestselling memoir. Being Heumann follows Heumann as she leads more than 100 disabled people to take over the San Francisco Federal Building, kicking off a 28 day sit-in in 1977. The protestors form a tightly bound community, refusing to leave until the government enforces section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, which required all federal spaces to become accessible. Heder and Rebekah Tussing adapted the memoir. Mark Ruffalo, Dylan O’Brien, Jon Beavers, Rob Delaney, Ray Fisher and more star in the pic. David Permut, Heder, John W. Beach, Kevin Cleary and Kevin J. Walsh produce. Watch on Deadline ‘Prima Facie’ Prima Facie is the feature adaptation of the West End and Broadway play (which originally starred Jodie Comer). Erivo plays a British defense barrister who exudes enviable brilliance in navigating the ruthless and gladiatorial London courtrooms. She is formidable in her defense of men charged with sexual assault; but just as she is fast-tracking to stardom, the tide turns to crisis, and she must fight to define herself. Playwright Suzie Miller adapted her Olivier-winning and Tony-nominated play for the big screen. Deadline first told you about the project at Cannes 2025, when Embankment Films handled global sales with UTA Independent Film Group and CAA Media Finance co-representing domestic. The Assassin(s) is set in 1974 and follows the attempted assassination of Korean president Park Chung-hee on August 15 of that year — one of the most consequential days in the country’s history. Yoo Hae-jin, Park Hae-il and Lee Min-ho star. Park portrays a news editor who delves into unanswered questions surrounding the attempted assassination. Yoo is the police inspector, and Lee is a journalist both of whom witness the assassination. “We’re thrilled to open this year’s festival with Siân Heder’s inspiring follow-up to her Oscar-winning CODA ,” TIFF CEO Cameron Bailey said. “ Being Heumann features an electric performance from Ruth Madeley in the story of Judy Heumann, a world-changing advocate for accessibility. We’re also glad to reveal the news that Toronto audiences will be the first to see Cynthia Erivo in Susanna White’s searing legal drama Prima Facie , and that the South Korean power duo of director Hur Jin-ho and superstar Lee Min-ho will launch their thriller The Assassin(s) at our 51st festival. Lots more to come.” Being Heumann will debut on Thursday, September 10 at Roy Thomson Hall. Last year’s TIFF drew 700,000 attendees.
